findings.evidence: naming-conventions.md: "the namespace is prepended back to it in `lowerCamelCase`. This is to ensure that `_`-separated strings in a lemma name correspond to a definition name or connective." Contrast `card_injective_hom_eq_labelledCopyCount` in the same file.
findings.fix: Rename to `card_hom_eq_card_adjPreservingMaps` (update the module docstring at lines 69-70 and both uses in `StepGraphon/FiniteGraph/Examples.lean:57,67`).
findings.issue: `card_hom_eq_card_adj_preserving_maps` splits the prose "adjacency-preserving maps" into `_`-separated segments that correspond to no declaration, and breaks symmetry with the equiv it is the cardinality form of (`homEquivAdjPreservingMaps`, line 170) and with the adjacent `card_injective_hom_eq_labelledCopyCount` (line 148), which spells the referenced object in lowerCamelCase.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:109,114,122,129,138 — four `finiteGraphGraphon_apply*` lemmas; only this one names a hypothesis unrelated to the cells, and `m` is implicit in the statement.
findings.fix: Name it after what it says rather than after the hypothesis, e.g. `finiteGraphGraphon_apply_fin` (the value in terms of `G.Adj` on `Fin m`), leaving `finiteGraphGraphon_apply` as the `ℕ`-level defining equation.
findings.issue: `finiteGraphGraphon_apply_of_pos` is the general `Fin m`-level evaluation lemma (and the `@[simp]` one the docstring tells callers to use, line 85), but `_of_pos` names a hypothesis on the implicit `m`, which does not appear in the left-hand side. Its three siblings `_of_adj`, `_of_not_adj`, `_of_cellIdx_eq` all name cell hypotheses instead, so the suffix does not distinguish the general form from the cell-conditioned one; the PR's other `0 < m` lemmas (`cellIdx_lt`, `integral_pi_comp_cellIdx`, `homDensity_finiteGraphGraphon`) put no suffix in the name at all.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Pi.lean:106,115,119,124 — `integral_fintype_prod_eq_prod`, `integral_fintype_prod_eq_pow`, etc., all carry the RHS in the name.
findings.issue: `integral_pi_comp_cellIdx` names only the left-hand side; the conclusion is that the integral equals a finite sum over `V → Fin m` divided by `m ^ card V`, which the name does not advertise. Mathlib's lemmas of exactly this shape name the right-hand side.

summary: No notation is introduced and the roadmap-pinned names are honored, but three names break the naming conventions or local symmetry: a snake-cased prose segment in `card_hom_eq_card_adj_preserving_maps`, an uninformative `_of_pos` on the main evaluation lemma, and a transfer lemma whose name hides its right-hand side.
